prompt: A shop offers a ten-percent discount on an item and then adds ten percent to the reduced price. Explain why the result is not the original price, using an item priced at 100 units. Keep your response near 80 words.
text: An item priced at 100 units receives a 10% discount, subtracting 10 units and leaving 90 units. Adding 10% to that reduced price adds only 9 units, because the increase is calculated from 90, not 100. The final price is therefore 99 units, which is 1 unit below the original price. The percentages do not cancel because they apply to different amounts: the discount uses the original price, while the increase uses the smaller, discounted price.
